name: MATRIX SERVICE

priced.reason: not a repriceable fcff name or no growth supplied

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That I am refusing a name whose operating turnaround is now demonstrated rather than promised — three consecutive profitable quarters, gross margin up 150bp to 8.2%, SG&A down $3.0M on a completed restructuring, adjusted EBITDA tripled to $7.7M, a debt-free balance sheet and $221.8M of liquidity — and that $68.5M of enterprise value for $872.6M of backlog plus an $8.2bn opportunity pipeline is cheap on any reading. On this telling the negative operating cash flow is first-quarter seasonality (the company prepays annual insurance premiums in Q1 and says so) plus a $23.2M accounts-payable decrease, not deterioration.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: How much of the $182.4M of unrestricted cash survives working the backlog off. That is the whole question, and it decides the sign.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Partly, and it cuts both ways, which is why the verdict holds. For the counter: the 10-Q does attribute part of the outflow to the Q1 insurance prepayment and to a $23.2M payables decrease, and accounts receivable actually DECREASED $4.9M, so this is not a collections failure. Against the counter, and decisively on the point that matters: the company earned $6.2M of net income and consumed $37.0M of cash in the same quarter, and the prior-year Q1 was also negative ($25.9M), so Q1 seasonality does not explain a $11.1M year-over-year deterioration on higher revenue and better margins. The float fell $8.9M, which is the direction the last pass predicted. And backlog fell a further 8.5% sequentially on a 0.6x book-to-bill — so the work that would rebuild the float is not being won yet, notice to proceed notwithstanding.
devils_advocate.unresolved: Still the distributable cash, and I now think it is structurally unanswerable from the filings: the 10-Q presents liquidity ($221.8M) and the contract liability ($291.0M) but never nets them, and management gives no fiscal 2027 guidance to anchor the revenue decline a 0.6x book-to-bill implies. I also cannot tell whether the $20.0M retention release is a one-off or the start of a working-capital unlock. The `operating_leases_26%_of_EV` flag remains real and, on a $68.5M enterprise value, material on its own.

what_changed: The test the 2026-10-23 pass nominated has now run, and it answered in that pass's favour. That pass wrote: 'Quarterly BIE and net contract liabilities: continued decline confirms the float is reversing and operating cash flow stays near zero.' The Q1 FY2027 10-Q filed 2026-11-05 reports BIE down from $299,947k to $290,998k and net contract liabilities down from $(270,716)k to $(262,016)k — and operating cash flow of NEGATIVE $36,958k, against negative $25,899k a year earlier. Not 'near zero': materially negative, and worse than the comparable quarter. Unrestricted cash fell $40.6M in the quarter, from $222,966k to $182,381k. Meanwhile the reported result improved: revenue $219.4M (from $211.9M), gross margin 8.2% (from 6.7%), net income $6.2M or $0.22 a share against a prior-year loss of $(0.13), adjusted EBITDA $7.7M against $2.5M — a third consecutive profitable quarter. And backlog fell again, to $872.6M from $953.2M, on awards of $138.8M and a book-to-bill of 0.6x, the second consecutive quarter below 1.0x. Still no fiscal 2027 guidance. A $20.0M project letter of credit released $20.0M of contract retention, and ABL availability fell to $39.4M on a $61.8M borrowing base.
consensus_case: The market is paying $242.0M for a heavy industrial contractor holding $182.4M of unrestricted cash and no debt, i.e. roughly $60M for the operating business — and it is right to, because the cash is not the shareholders'. Against that $182.4M sit $291.0M of billings on uncompleted contracts in excess of costs (BIE) that must be worked off in labour and materials, $25.0M of restricted cash the ABL covenant will not release, and $22.4M of letters of credit. The market's -46.2% implied growth is not a forecast of collapse; it is the arithmetic consequence of the engine deducting customer money from enterprise value. Priced on what the business actually earns — Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA of $7.7M, annualising near $31M — the equity is on roughly 14x after-tax owner earnings with a 0.6x book-to-bill and a backlog falling. That is a full price, not a cheap one.
base_case_rationale: No number is recordable, for the reason the 2026-10-23 pass gave and which this quarter strengthens rather than resolves: enterprise value is indeterminate within a factor of about five, and the sign of the answer sits inside that range. The engine's $68.5M enterprise value deducts $182.4M of cash as though it were the shareholders'; if the $262.0M net contract liability is instead treated as a claim, enterprise value is nearer $330M. The $59.3M FCFF base is the same error on the income side: it is the mean of cfo-less-capex of [$1.4M, $109.8M, $65.6M], where the two large years were supplied by the float ($152.3M and $85.9M of BIE inflow against $117.5M and $72.6M of operating cash flow — more than 100% in both), and the newest year of $1.4M is the only one that is not float. The HOG/JBI cross-check now fires harder than it did three weeks ago: the $59.3M base is about 1.9x the company's own annualised adjusted EBITDA of roughly $31M, and 3.7x fiscal 2026's actual $16.0M. A growth rate applied to that base is meaningless in either direction.
key_risks: Q1 FY27 operating cash flow was NEGATIVE $37.0M on net income of +$6.2M, and unrestricted cash fell $40.6M in one quarter — reported profit is not cash at this company
Backlog fell to $872.6M from $953.2M with a 0.6x book-to-bill, the second consecutive quarter below 1.0x, so both revenue and the float shrink from here

Enterprise value is indeterminate within a factor of about five: the $182.4M of cash the model deducts is largely the $291.0M of customer billings it must work off, $25.0M is covenant-restricted and $22.4M of LCs are outstanding
The FCFF base of $59.3M is roughly 1.9x annualised adjusted EBITDA and 3.7x fiscal 2026's actual $16.0M, which is arithmetically impossible for a business also paying taxes and capex
ABL availability is only $39.4M on a $61.8M borrowing base, so the cash balance is the liquidity, and it is falling
No fiscal 2027 guidance, and both the CEO and CFO are new (CFO appointed 2026-10-19)
watch_for: Q2 FY27 operating cash flow: a second consecutive large negative quarter would confirm the float unwind is structural rather than seasonal, and would take cash below $150M
Book-to-bill above 1.0x on a total-company basis, and whether the data-centre power notice to proceed and the America First Refining FEED convert to funded backlog
Any fiscal 2027 revenue or adjusted EBITDA guidance — currently none exists
Whether the engine ever gates a cash-flow base against the company's own adjusted EBITDA; the HOG/JBI check would have stopped this name before selection for a second time
